title: Dropbox access token as a Bearer header value or the access_token response member
summary: A synthetic opaque value after the Bearer scheme in a raw request and a quoted curl -H argument, and as the access_token member of a pretty-printed and of a compact token response that also carries expires_in.
rationale: Dropbox documents that authorized requests carry an Authorization header with the value Bearer followed by the access token, and that the token endpoint response has an access_token member beside expires_in (contract claims access-token-exists and token-response-member-opaque). Dropbox says the token is opaque, may exceed 1KB and has no guaranteed size or composition (access-token-documented-opaque), so the value is flagged because of where it sits, not because of its shape; no sl. prefix or length is used. The extent is the value only. expires_in is metadata.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in an Authorization: Bearer header or the access_token member of a Dropbox token response is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Dropbox documents the Bearer Authorization header and the access_token response member (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: Authorized requests to the API should use an Authorization header with the value Bearer <TOKEN>, where <TOKEN> is an access token obtained through the OAuth flow.
The access token to be used to call the Dropbox API. This should always be treated as opaque with no guarantees as to the size or composition of this token.
The length of time in seconds that the access token will be valid for.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
